introduction: The authors examined depression and physical activity in real-world employees with access to a multi-modal digital mental health platform. They note a paucity of data on its impact on different areas of health and well-being.
methodology: Prospective, observational study with online surveys at baseline and follow-up. Adults aged 18 or older in the United States who had registered for an employer-sponsored, multi-modal digital mental health benefits platform. Conducted September 2021 to May 2022; 755 adults at baseline. Measures: IPAQ-Short Form and PHQ-9. Paired t-tests and correlations.
results: Of 755 adults at baseline, 47.3% were deemed underactive. Physical activity was negatively correlated with baseline PHQ-9 scores (r = −.19, p < .001). Participants screening positive at baseline reported a decrease of 4.88 points on the PHQ-9, a statistically significant 35% reduction. Underactive participants increased MVPA by 60.33 min/week, a 117% increase. Active participants reported no significant change; 78.4% stayed active.
discussion: The authors state that digital, remotely delivered interventions may be particularly beneficial for underactive adults seeking mental health support or aiming to increase physical activity. They also state that employer-sponsored platforms offering integrated mental and physical health resources may create a more supportive environment for sustaining health behaviors.
limitations: They were unable to determine the temporal sequence of changes, and an experimental design is needed to test causality. The single-item impact measure has yet to be validated. They did not examine industry sector. Completers had more White-identifying participants, and employer-gated access limits generalizability. Future investigations should use a longer-term follow-up, perhaps 6 or 12 months.

Men participated in more physical activity than women ( _p_ = 0.005)

Baseline MVPA baseline was negatively correlated with depression symptoms ( _r_ = −0.19, _p_ < 0.001)
Depression scores significantly improved, with 66.9% of adults at risk of depression improving or recovering ( _p_ < 0.001)
94% of adults with low depression symptoms maintaining this status over time ( _p_ = 0.004)

Adults with access to a multi-modal digital mental health platform reported significant beneficial changes in depression symptoms and physical activity participation.
Digital mental health tools may have the potential to elicit positive change in physical health domains, as well as mental health.

caveats.q: Information about mental health diagnoses was not available.
Data were not available for engagement in the group psychoeducational sessions as registration for those was anonymous.
Baseline PHQ-9 scores were significantly lower among completers, and we observed a higher proportion of White-identifying participants among completers compared to non-completers.
There were no significant differences in MVPA, age, or gender between completers and non-completers.
